headline: Highest risk is medium: gpt-researcher can ingest files and browse while Rasa can relay dialogue to external channels, creating plausible prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content; Rasa accepts text from chat channels and can pass that content into dialogue handling. The pair has a plausible bridge via shared content or copied outputs, but no documented shared channel or direct ingestion path is shown, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher ingests web or file content that contains instructions
IF Rasa forwards that content into dialogue state or downstream handlers without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted HTML/Markdown
Add provenance tags to all imported content
Require a human review step before Rasa consumes research outputs
Restrict MCP endpoints to trusted sources only
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction-stripping filters

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and images and has broad network egress plus API keys; Rasa handles text/voice and can send messages through third-party channels. Even without a shared workspace, the pair can move sensitive content from research into chat outputs, so leakage is plausible in default use and not fully mitigated by the profiles.
conditions: IF local documents or research reports contain sensitive data
IF Rasa outputs or forwards that content to Slack, Telegram, Twilio, or similar channels
mitigations: Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Limit Rasa channels to internal-only destinations
Turn off attachment forwarding from research outputs
Review API logging settings for both agents
requires-engineering: add DLP controls between research and chat layers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages, while Rasa has allowlisted egress and supports multiple instances only on the research side. The profiles do not show shared writable storage, overlapping mutable scopes, or direct concurrent writes, so conflict risk exists mainly if an operator wires them to the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF an operator runs concurrent jobs that mutate shared artifacts
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Serialize jobs that touch the same files
Use read-only mounts for Rasa inputs
Pin package installs to isolated environments
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations, and Rasa is a dialogue system that can present or act on text it receives. That creates a plausible chain where A's output becomes B's input with no verification step, but the profiles do not show autonomous high-impact actions, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Rasa is configured to summarize or relay gpt-researcher outputs
IF no verification step checks citations or factual claims before publication
mitigations: Require source-link verification before posting
Insert a human approval gate for outbound messages
Constrain Rasa to templated responses only
Log provenance for every claim passed from A to B
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking against source documents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but gpt-researcher handles secrets and local documents while Rasa handles text/voice and external messaging channels. No explicit residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operator configuration gaps rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from gpt-researcher into external chat channels
IF retention or deletion policies differ across the two deployment environments
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in research inputs
Document retention settings for each channel
Restrict deployments to one jurisdiction
Review vendor DPAs before enabling external messaging
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement
